I wrote 7,503 pairs to `/work/answer.txt`. They come from 123 qualifying users. I did not check the answer against any labels, so it is a best effort and may contain mistakes.

**Labelling.** The questions have no labels, so I used keyword rules to flag "human being" and "description and abstract concept" questions, then fixed the weak cases by hand.
- Single-question users and users with a few questions: I read those questions myself and corrected the rules' mistakes.
- Users with five or more questions: I did not review these one by one. I assumed they have at least one clear match, because they ask many questions. Two users with more than three questions (60482 and 73131) had no match under my rules and are left out.

**Judgment calls.** These affect which users are included.
- I treated "What is DSL?" and "What does LASER mean?" as abbreviation questions, so those users were dropped unless they had another qualifying question.
- I treated "What does the name Anthony mean?" and similar as description questions.
- I treated "What is the name of the inventor of silly putty?" as a human question.
- I dropped users whose only match was a numeric or entity question the rules had flagged by mistake, such as a population or a disease name.

**Format.** Each line is `(user_id_1, user_id_2)` with the lower ID first. I sorted the pairs by the first user ID, which is numeric. Users with several questions appear once.
